subject: Why doesn't mutate_each work for one function

messages.author: 8b446c107e0878a8
messages.subject: Why doesn't mutate_each work for one function
parts:
Hi,

I have this example dataframe:
S <- data_frame(Group = rep( letters[1:3], 10),
                X = rep( c( 10, 20, 40), 10) + rnorm( 30, 0, 1),
                Y = rep( c( 10, 30, 90), 10) + rnorm( 30, 0, 1),
                Z = rep( c(10, 40, 160), 10) +rnorm(30, 0, 1) )

If I run:
S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(avg=mean(.,na.rm=T)),X:Z)
I expect 3 new avg columns to appear but nothing happens.

If I however add a second function:
S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(avg=mean(.,na.rm=T),centered= . - mean(.,na.rm=T)),X:Z)
everything works as I expected.

Is this a bug?

Greetings
  Robert

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Why doesn't mutate_each work for one function
parts:
> If I run:
> S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(avg=mean(.,na.rm=T)),X:Z)
> I expect 3 new avg columns to appear but nothing happens.

Well, something happens, but it's not what you expect - the old
columns are replaced with the new ones. I think the problem is
basically the default names that mutate_each() picks.

Hadley

parts:
Alain wrote:
S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(avg=mean(.,na.rm=T)), Avg= X:Z)

I could work with that although I have to rename the new columns or do:
S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(avg=mean(.,na.rm=T)), Avg_X= X,Avg_Y= Y,Avg_Z= Z)

But I don't find it very logical.
I think this should change the existing columns:
S %>% group_by(Group) %>% mutate_each(funs(mean(.,na.rm=T)), X:Z)
And this should create new columns:
